targets.question: Enumerate the major publicly documented Beth Din corruption, misconduct, coercion, conflict-of-interest, retaliation, financial-abuse, procedural-abuse, and cover-up cases across multiple jurisdictions, with each claim separated into proven/adjudicated, documented, alleged, disputed, or unverified status.
targets.avoid: No collective blame, no race framing, and no allegation may be promoted to fact without supporting records.

targets.question: Resolve exact Beth Din institutions, aliases, jurisdictions, affiliations, judges/dayanim, administrators, parent organizations, governance structures, and civil courts that review or enforce their decisions.
required_evidence: official Beth Din pages and rules
targets.avoid: Do not merge unrelated tribunals merely because they use the generic label Beth Din.

targets.question: Trace documented fee flows, undisclosed financial relationships, self-dealing, repeat-player relationships, governance conflicts, recusal failures, and other conflicts of interest tied to Beth Din proceedings or administration.
targets.avoid: Do not infer corruption from ordinary fees, donations, professional relationships, or communal affiliation alone.

targets.question: Enumerate documented cases involving coercion, retaliation, extortionate conduct, blacklisting, threats, or abuse of communal leverage connected to Beth Din get/divorce proceedings, and distinguish lawful pressure, disputed conduct, civil findings, and criminal findings.
targets.avoid: Do not characterize coercion as proven where the record only contains an accusation.

targets.question: Enumerate civil-court decisions enforcing, vacating, limiting, criticizing, sanctioning, or otherwise reviewing Beth Din arbitration awards and procedures, then classify the exact basis for each outcome.
targets.avoid: Do not treat routine vacatur or jurisdictional rulings as proof of corruption unless the court actually found misconduct.

targets.question: Identify recurring judges/dayanim, administrators, attorneys, intermediaries, organizations, and complainants across independent Beth Din misconduct cases and test whether the recurrence reflects an actual documented pattern rather than simple institutional prominence.
targets.avoid: Do not infer wrongdoing from repeated appearance alone.

targets.question: Compare Beth Din appointment, recusal, appeal, complaint, transparency, fee, evidence, publication, and oversight rules against the misconduct case ledger to identify governance weaknesses actually supported by multiple cases.
targets.avoid: Do not claim systemic corruption from structural weakness alone; separate corruption risk from proven corruption.

targets.question: After the Beth Din corpus is mature, enumerate comparable documented corruption or abuse cases in Islamic/Sharia councils, Christian ecclesiastical courts, canon-law tribunals, and other faith-based arbitration bodies to identify recurring governance patterns.
required_evidence: high-quality investigative reporting linked to primary documents
targets.avoid: Keep this a secondary governance comparison. Do not turn the dig into generic criticism of religion or demographic groups.
